My land is small — only 1.8 mu — but I have five mouths to feed and I've worked this ground for 20 years. I know what it needs.

I split my field the way I always do. I put about 1 mu into wheat and maize rotation — wheat in autumn, maize after the wheat comes off in June. The other 0.8 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton prices have been unsteady lately but I know how to grow it, and it gives me cash when maize doesn't.

For wheat, I'll rotary till after this year's maize harvest in October, then plant an improved variety — the seed station in the county sells the same ones my neighbors use, and they perform reliably. I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting and come back with urea at jointing. I irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Two rounds of pesticide — one for aphids in spring, one more if I see disease. I expect about 400 jin per mu.

For maize, I go straight into the stubble with no-till after wheat harvest — saves time and I need to get the seed in fast before the heat peaks. I use hybrid seed, always have for the past decade. I topdress nitrogen when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations if rain is short. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

For cotton, I prepare the seedbed in April with rotary tillage, then transplant seedlings in May. I use hybrid Bt cotton — it cuts down on bollworm spraying though I still spray six times through the season for aphids and mites. Cotton drinks water, so I irrigate four times. I put on more potassium than the other crops because I've learned it makes the bolls set better. I expect about 240 jin of seed cotton per mu.
